pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:308 The run.start audit is the only call record the runtime writes for an agent job. It stores the engine, the mode and the playbook's enum name, but no digest or size of the opening prompt or the playbook text actually sent, so 'what was this run told?' cannot be answered from artifacts once prompts/*.md changes between builds.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:308 'Record what was sent, at the send site' says to persist a fingerprint, size and content digest per prompt. Only a playbook name is recorded, and the playbook's compiled-in text can change under the same name. A grep of table-engine also found no prompt digest.

crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:256 The call site gives the engine typed inputs: a serialized projection or brief plus a Playbook enum. It never concatenates prompt text, and the system layer is chosen by table_engine::system_prompt.

crates/table-runtime/src/agent_surface_tests.rs:115 Trust is settled when the input is declared: the task input is a closed typed projection that cannot represent counterparty prose. The test checks that leak strings are absent and that the prompt parses back into AgentProjection.

crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:255 The injected table is reachable material (the same projection table_view returns), so it saves tool calls and cannot disagree with what the agent would fetch itself.

crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:131 The engines are external agent harnesses (claude-code, codex-cli) that hold their own transcript. The runtime sends only the opening job and never edits or compacts history, which matches the agent-held regime.
crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:263 The clock is read once per run into the one-shot task layer, not into a cached system layer that is re-sent across a long session.
